prompt:
A flat, matte design sketch of a desktop website homepage, landscape 16:9, shown straight on with no perspective, no device frame, no browser chrome, no drop shadows, no gloss, no photorealism. Deliberately unfinished, like a designer's layout study rendered in flat color blocks.

Palette, used exactly: warm aged-paper off-white background (#F7F3ED), dark warm ink (#2A231C), one muted slate blue accent (#365778), and a deep near-black warm brown (#171310) for a few solid blocks. No other colors. A faint regular dot grid over the paper background.

There are no photographs, no screenshots, no user interface chrome and no browser windows anywhere. Everything is typography and simple ruled shapes.

Composition, top to bottom:

A thin quiet header strip across the very top with the word Narraitor small on the left.

A serif headline across the left half reading exactly: Play a story in any world you can imagine

Then the body of the page: three large paired rows stacked vertically, each row separated from the next by a thick horizontal rule with clear space around it. Each row is split into two unequal columns.

The LEFT column of each row is narrow, about one third of the width, and sits on a solid deep near-black warm brown block with generous padding. Inside it, in pale text against the dark block: a small greeked tag at the top, then three or four SHORT greeked lines, deliberately sparse and ragged, standing in for the handful of words someone typed.

The RIGHT column of each row is wide, about two thirds, on the plain paper background. Inside it: a large bold greeked heading bar at the top, then eight or nine soft indistinct horizontal lines of full measure standing in for a generated passage of prose. This side is visibly dense and full where the left side is sparse.

Between the two columns of each row, place a small slate blue arrow or triangle marker pointing from left to right, centred vertically.

The three rows should feel visibly different from each other in the length and ragged shape of their left-hand lines, so the page reads as three different worlds.

At the bottom, a compact solid slate-blue rectangular button on the left, and a thin footer strip with three small greeked links.

The only legible text anywhere is the word Narraitor and the headline. Every other text region is greeked: indistinct horizontal bars standing in for words, not real letters. Do not render invented prices, dates, statistics, logos, faces, or photographs.

The overall feeling is a printed before-and-after comparison sheet: a few sparse words on the dark side, a full page of writing on the light side, three times over.
